mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising from their collapsed levels, weekday footfall should recover and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace and transit mobility stall or reverse before retail catches up.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rising for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary trips into outdoor activity and signals broader relaxation of stay-at-home behavior, which then spills into more retail visits within one to two weeks. The effect weakens if parks rebound without any concurrent easing in transit or workplace mobility.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week after a prior trough
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days after PARKS rises by 10 points or more week-on-week from a depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, commuting and shopping trips remain constrained and retail mobility continues to trend down over the next four weeks. This fails when transit recovers materially even though residential time is still high.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -60 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more essential errand circulation and normalizes short-distance travel, which should spill over into retail-and-recreation visits within one week. The signal fails if grocery mobility rises because of stockpiling while other activity categories keep falling.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES recover faster than TRANSIT, workers may shift to local errands after partial reopening, producing a retail rebound within two to four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace gains are not accompanied by any transit recovery, because commuting alone will not translate into shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds TRANSIT by at least 10 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its recent four-week average 28 days after WORKPLACES outpaces TRANSIT by 10 points or more for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stops rising and begins to fall, time spent at home is being replaced by out-of-home activity, which should push retail mobility upward over the next two weeks. The effect fails if the residential pullback is caused by survey noise while transit, workplaces, and parks stay flat.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 3 points week-on-week after being above 25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops by 3 points or more from a level above 25.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates general mobility normalization after a weather or calendar shock, and retail visits follow with a one-week lag. The signal fails if parks rise only because people substitute away from indoor retail and grocery mobility weakens at the same time.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two straight weeks while GROCERY_PHARM does not fall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher in the next 7 days after PARKS rises for two weeks and GROCERY_PHARM is non-declining.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a renewed decline in TRANSIT together with weak WORKPLACES mobility will keep retail mobility below its recent average over the next four weeks. This mechanism fails if retail stabilizes even though both commuter proxies remain depressed, implying demand has detached from commuting constraints.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls back below -70 while WORKPLACES stays below -60
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT remains below -70 and WORKPLACES remains below -60.
